summary: Autoplay's prewarm now gets a 60s lead time instead of 12s, so a slow related() lookup actually finishes before the track ends.
details: Live incident (2026-09-02): the new autoplay instrumentation caught the real mechanism directly in production logs. The prewarm's related() Mix lookup measured 38.4s under real contention against the shared yt-dlp extractor -- far past the old 12s lead time. The prewarm was still in flight when the track's natural end fired the live fallback, which raced the SAME contended extractor and came back genuinely empty in under a second; by the time the prewarm's own (correct, 48-candidate) answer landed, the chain had already given up and gone idle, and the stale-pick guard silently discarded a valid pick.

Raised autoplay_prewarm_seconds from 12.0 to 60.0 in the deployed config -- real margin above the one measured worst case. Tracks shorter than that still fall back to the existing at-end lookup, unchanged.
The stale-pick discard in _prewarm_pick now logs what it threw away, so a recurrence is visible instead of indistinguishable from 'related() found nothing'.
limitations: This raises the lead time rather than fixing the underlying related()-call latency/contention or the discard-on-stale race itself -- a track shorter than 60s, or a lookup slower than the new margin, can still lose the race. The added logging will surface that if it recurs.
